claims.text: An actively learned moment tensor potential can reproduce ab initio free-energy landscapes for both solid and liquid phases of multicomponent high-entropy alloys.
The MTP framework can faithfully retain vibrational entropy, anharmonicity, and electron–vibration coupling.
The framework will reduce computational cost by at least an order of magnitude relative to full AIMD and TOR-TILD workflows.
CoCrFeNi and CoCrFeNiTa alloys have complex configurational disorder.
The proposed high-entropy-alloy systems exhibit significant anharmonic vibrational behavior.
Active learning can construct property- and system-tailored MTP training sets using a minimal amount of ab initio data.
Active learning can identify and sample thermodynamically critical configurations, particularly configurations near phase boundaries.
TOR-TILD becomes computationally prohibitive for compositions typical of multicomponent high-entropy alloys.
Moment tensor descriptors encode local atomic environments and short- to mid-range ordering fluctuations.
The descriptor-encoded local environments mediate vibrational-entropy, anharmonic, and electron–vibration contributions.
Iterative training on targeted ab initio configurations allows an MTP to interpolate relevant free-energy surfaces efficiently.
Targeted active learning reduces the need for exhaustive full AIMD sampling.
MTP predictions of phase free energies, melting temperatures, and latent heats will remain within 5–10% of explicit ab initio results.
Explicit AIMD and TOR-TILD workflows fully sample phase free energies with all relevant entropy contributions.
The proposed method is primarily applicable to multicomponent high-entropy alloys from near melting into the liquid regime.
Extreme anharmonicity or strongly nonlinear electron–vibration coupling may reduce the method's reliability.
A deviation greater than approximately 10% from AIMD or TOR-TILD across multiple compositions and temperatures would falsify the hypothesis.
